samples.summary: Docs toolbar asks the Font Loading API without awaiting the new `ensureFontLink` promise, so it can resolve against the subset preview face and poison `FontRegistry`'s per-family cache permanently
samples.evidence:
`ensureFont` (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-formatting-toolbar.tsx:345-355) does `ensureFontLink(family);` and then, synchronously, `store.fonts?.ensureFont?.(family)`. That reaches `FontRegistry.ensureFont` in packages/docs/src/view/fonts.ts:293-314, whose FIRST act is `document.fonts.check('12px "Family"')` (line 302) and, when it answers true, `this.status.set(key, 'loaded'); return;` — with NO `onFontLoaded` listeners fired, and the status cached for the lifetime of the registry.

This diff is what makes that reachable: the same toolbar renders `FontFamilyPicker` (lines 446, 643, 709), whose in-view observer now injects a `&text=` subset link for every visible row (packages/frontend/src/components/text-formatting/font-family-picker.tsx:149). A `&text=` response carries no `unicode-range`, so — by the diff's own reasoning in font-catalog.ts:155-160 and :218-222 — `check()`/`load()` match it for the family. Hovering or picking a previewed row therefore hits `check() === true` against the label-only subset, marks the family 'loaded' forever, and never notifies the canvas re-layout listeners. Docs text then renders with only the glyphs the picker row painted (or a fallback) and never repaints, and the docs PDF export inherits the same registry state.

`pdf-actions.ts` was fixed by awaiting the promise; this call site was not. Fix belongs here (await `ensureFontLink(family)` before `store.fonts.ensureFont`), or in `FontRegistry` so a subset face cannot satisfy `check()`.

samples.summary: Slides family-apply calls `document.fonts.load` immediately after the now-async `ensureFontLink`, so it can resolve against the subset preview face and repaint the dirty-gated canvas exactly once, with the wrong glyphs
samples.evidence: packages/frontend/src/app/slides/toolbar/apply-font-family.ts:28-39: `ensureFontLink(family);` (promise dropped) then `document.fonts.load(`16px ${JSON.stringify(family)}`).then(() => { editor.markDirty(); editor.render(); })`. Since this change, the family the user just picked normally already has a `&text=` subset link in the head (injected by the picker's in-view observer, packages/frontend/src/components/text-formatting/font-family-picker.tsx:149), and a subset face has no `unicode-range`, so `load()` resolves instantly against it. The single `markDirty`/`render` then fires against the label-only face; because the slides renderer is dirty-gated (see the comment at apply-font-family.ts:17-21), nothing repaints when the real family finally arrives — the canvas keeps the wrong glyphs until an unrelated edit. Both slides toolbars route through this helper (text-edit-section.tsx:65ff, mobile-toolbar.tsx:549ff). The fix is to await the returned promise, as `pdf-actions.ts` now does.

samples.summary: Theme font setter fires `ensureFontLink` without awaiting it, so the theme is applied while the family's only connected face may be a label-only preview subset
samples.evidence: packages/frontend/src/app/slides/theme-builder-panel.tsx:99-102 `setFont` does `ensureFontLink(family); store.batch(... updateTheme ...)`. The panel renders `FontFamilyPicker` (lines 172, 179), so the picked family will usually already have a `&text=` subset link injected by the new preview observer. Any measurement/paint that happens on the resulting store update sees the subset face first; unlike the other call sites there is no explicit `fonts.load` here, so the impact depends on how the slides renderer reacts to the theme change — I could not confirm a repaint is scheduled once the full face lands.

samples.summary: The ~1,900-entry full-catalog chunk is now dynamically imported on plain dropdown open (not only on the "More fonts…" dialog), for every picker mount whose recents include a non-curated family
samples.evidence: packages/frontend/src/components/text-formatting/font-family-picker.tsx:95-104: the effect gate became `if (!moreOpen && !(open && needFullForRecents)) return;`, where `needFullForRecents` is true whenever any localStorage recent is absent from `CATALOG_BY_FAMILY`. Recents are written as bare family names by `packages/frontend/src/components/text-formatting/font-recents.ts` (KEY `wafflebase:recent-fonts`), so one pick from the full library permanently flips this on. Every consumer of the picker then pays the extra chunk fetch just for opening the dropdown — docs mounts three of them (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-formatting-toolbar.tsx:446, 643, 709) plus slides desktop/mobile toolbars. `loadFullFontCatalog` is memoized (font-catalog-full-loader.ts:12-23) so it is one network fetch, but it is a fetch on a path that previously had none.

samples.summary: `ensureFontLink`'s already-requested branch can hand back an immediately-resolved promise for a stylesheet still in flight, so the awaiting PDF-export path can proceed against an unloaded (or subset-only) face
samples.evidence: packages/frontend/src/components/text-formatting/font-catalog.ts:178-181 returns `fullLinkSettled.get(existing) ?? Promise.resolve()` — the fallback is documented as an HMR-only case, but the WeakMap is module state and every other consumer of the module (`packages/frontend/src/app/slides/toolbar/text-edit-section.tsx:68` and `mobile-toolbar.tsx:554` pass `ensureFontLink` straight to `onPrefetch`, so hover injects the link long before the export runs) resolves through the same module instance, so this only degrades after a reload. Worth naming because the awaiting caller added in this change (`pdf-actions.ts:47-50`) treats a resolved promise as proof the face is connected, and in that branch it is not — and no subset removal happens either, since `removePreviewFontLink` only runs on the original injection's settle.

verdict.reason: The unawaited `ensureFontLink(family)` at docs-formatting-toolbar.tsx:350 is real, but the claimed consequence cannot occur. The next line, `store.fonts?.ensureFont?.(family)` (docs-formatting-toolbar.tsx:351-354), is a permanent no-op: `EditorAPI.getStore()` (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:55) returns a `DocStore`, and neither implementation exposes a `fonts` member — `YorkieDocStore` (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:549-564, which is what docs-view.tsx:324-327 constructs) nor `MemDocStore` (packages/docs/src/store/memory.ts:32); a grep for `fonts` in packages/docs/src/store and in yorkie-doc-store.ts returns nothing, and no site assigns `.fonts =`. `FontRegistry` is never instantiated in production anywhere in the repo — the only `new FontRegistry()` is packages/docs/test/view/fonts.test.ts:63 — so there is no per-family status cache to poison and no `onFontLoaded` subscriber to starve. Independently, docs canvas re-layout does not depend on `FontRegistry` at all: packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:2663-2692 clears the measure cache, invalidates layout and re-renders on `document.fonts` `loadingdone`/`ready`, so the full face arriving does repaint; and `ensureFontLink` removes the subset link on settle (font-catalog.ts:191-198), so a subset face is not left authoritative. Docs PDF export loads faces itself (packages/docs/src/export/pdf-exporter.ts:251-256) and reads no registry state. The protected operation is thus guarded out of reach by the optional chain over an absent field.

finding.evidence: packages/frontend/src/app/slides/toolbar/apply-font-family.ts:28-39: `ensureFontLink(family);` (promise dropped) then `document.fonts.load(`16px ${JSON.stringify(family)}`).then(() => { editor.markDirty(); editor.render(); })`. Since this change, the family the user just picked normally already has a `&text=` subset link in the head (injected by the picker's in-view observer, packages/frontend/src/components/text-formatting/font-family-picker.tsx:149), and a subset face has no `unicode-range`, so `load()` resolves instantly against it. The single `markDirty`/`render` then fires against the label-only face; because the slides renderer is dirty-gated (see the comment at apply-font-family.ts:17-21), nothing repaints when the real family finally arrives — the canvas keeps the wrong glyphs until an unrelated edit. Both slides toolbars route through this helper (text-edit-section.tsx:65ff, mobile-toolbar.tsx:549ff). The fix is to await the returned promise, as `pdf-actions.ts` now does.

verdict.reason: Verified in the repo: apply-font-family.ts:28 drops the promise now returned by ensureFontLink and calls document.fonts.load at :32-33 immediately, with a single markDirty/render at :35-36 on a renderer the file's own comment (:18-21) describes as dirty-gated. ensureFontLink's contract explicitly requires the opposite (font-catalog.ts:155-160: "AWAIT IT BEFORE document.fonts.load()/check()… this family's &text= face"), and the subset face is only dropped on stylesheet settle (font-catalog.ts:191-198), so it is still connected — and, per the picker's in-view observer (font-family-picker.tsx:149 -> ensurePreviewFontLink, font-catalog.ts:305-331, no unicode-range), normally present for the family just picked. The sibling caller pdf-actions.ts:47-58 was updated to await it and documents this exact hazard, so this is an unupdated caller of a changed contract. The slides editor's document.fonts 'loadingdone' listener (packages/slides/src/view/editor/editor.ts:1062-1069) is a partial mitigation only: canvas paints do not trigger font loads and nothing re-issues load() for the full face, so recovery depends incidentally on DOM text pulling the right unicode-range subsets. Not enough to refute. Both slides toolbars reach it (text-edit-section.tsx:67, mobile-toolbar.tsx:549ff), making it reachable and in-lane (changed contract, unupdated caller).

finding.summary: `verify:frame` is the one build-staleness gate left un-updated: it still rebuilds only `dist/shell`, yet it boots the fixture consumer whose vite.config imports the package BY NAME (→ `dist/plugin/index.js`)
finding.evidence: The diff fixed exactly this in `verify-consumer.mjs`, `verify-scenes.mjs`, `verify-tokens.mjs` and `scripts/design.mjs`, but `packages/design-editor/scripts/verify-frame.mjs:82-91` still runs only `vite build --config ./vite.shell.config.ts` and compares against `dist/shell/index.html` alone (`newestSourceMtime` at :95-108 also omits `tsconfig.build.json`). Its `boot()` at :118-124 starts vite on `PROJECT = packages/design-editor/fixtures/consumer` (:46), and `fixtures/consumer/vite.config.ts:17` does `import { designEditor, cssVariables } from '@wafflebase/design-editor'`, which `package.json:6-10` resolves to `./dist/plugin/index.js`. On a clean checkout (`dist/` is gitignored) the dev server dies with `Cannot find module …/dist/plugin/index.js`, reported as 'dev server exited early'; on a dirty one the browser gate runs against plugin bytes older than the change under test — the precise stale-bytes trap the diff's own comments say is 'worse than no gate'.

verdict.reason: The code is not as described. `verify-frame.mjs` contains no `vite build` call and no local `newestSourceMtime`; the cited lines :82-91 are `shutdown()` and the `boot()` dev-server `spawn`, and :95-108 is the health-poll loop. Instead, `verify-frame.mjs:43` imports `buildDesignEditorIfStale` from the shared `./build-if-stale.mjs` and calls it at `:122` before `boot()` — the same helper `verify-consumer.mjs:37,174` uses. That helper builds BOTH artefacts: `build-if-stale.mjs:40` lists `['dist/shell/index.html', 'dist/plugin/index.js']`, `:54` includes `tsconfig.build.json` in the mtime comparison, and `:74` runs the package's own `pnpm run build` (= `build:shell && build:plugin`, package.json:19-21), which produces the `./dist/plugin/index.js` that package.json:6-10 resolves the fixture's by-name import to. So neither failure mode claimed (clean checkout `Cannot find module`, dirty checkout stale plugin bytes) is reachable on this path. The reviewer appears to have read the past-tense narration at verify-frame.mjs:113-121 ("this gate used to rebuild only dist/shell") as current behaviour; that comment is the rationale immediately preceding the fix. A repo-wide Grep confirms only one verify-frame.mjs exists and no shell-only build path remains in it; the `verify-scenes.mjs`/`verify-tokens.mjs` named in the finding live in packages/design-sandbox/scripts and likewise already cover both artefacts (verify-scenes.mjs:92-95, verify-tokens.mjs:166-169).

finding.summary: Slides PDF export awaits `document.fonts.load(...)`, which can now resolve against a preview subset face while the full family stylesheet is still in flight, rasterising the deck with label-only glyphs
finding.evidence: `packages/frontend/src/app/slides/pdf-actions.ts:31-39` calls `ensureFontLink(family)` and then `await document.fonts.load('16px "family"')`. `document.fonts.load` only waits on faces already registered in the FontFaceSet; if the user previewed that family in the picker, a `&text=`-subset face (no `unicode-range`) is registered and loaded, so `load()` can resolve immediately while the just-injected full stylesheet has not been parsed, and `exportSlidesPdf` then measures/paints with the subset face. Previously previewing injected the full family, so this ordering hazard did not exist. Same shape at `packages/docs/src/export/pdf-exporter.ts:250-257` (mitigated there because Noto Sans/Serif KR are `eager: true`, so previews no-op for them).

verdict.reason: The claimed code shape is not in the tree. `exportSlidesPdfAndDownload` awaits the `ensureFontLink` promises before touching the Font Loading API: `await Promise.race([Promise.all(families.map(f => ensureFontLink(f))), timeout])` at packages/frontend/src/app/slides/pdf-actions.ts:47-50, with the `document.fonts.load` loop only afterwards at :51-59 (the cited lines 31-39 are JSDoc about images plus the function signature, not a fire-and-forget call). `ensureFontLink` (packages/frontend/src/components/text-formatting/font-catalog.ts:173-202) returns a promise that resolves on the link's load/error event — i.e. after the full family's @font-face rules parse — and its `.then()` calls `removePreviewFontLink(family)` (:197, impl :223-225), removing the `&text=` subset link so `document.fonts.load()` cannot resolve against it. The file's own header (:24-30) states this ordering explicitly as the reason for the wait. The secondary site is mitigated as the reviewer concedes: packages/docs/src/export/pdf-exporter.ts:250-257 only loads Noto Sans/Serif KR, both `eager: true` (font-catalog.data.ts:6-7), and `ensurePreviewFontLink` returns early for eager entries (font-catalog.ts:313), so no subset face exists for them.
